etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English restreinen, a borrowing from Old French restreindre, from Latin rēstringere (“fasten, tighten”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To control or keep in check.

quote.citation: 1875, Russell Thacher Trall, The Mother's Hygienic Hand-book, page 42:
quote.text: As with vicarious mismenstruation, the abnormal cessation only requires strict attention to the general health, with such measures to restrain hemorrhage as have already been indicated.

quote.citation: 2013 May 17, George Monbiot, “Money just makes the rich suffer”, in The Guardian Weekly‎[1], volume 188, number 23, page 19:
quote.text: In order to grant the rich these pleasures, the social contract is reconfigured. […]  The public realm is privatised, the regulations restraining the ultra-wealthy and the companies they control are abandoned, and Edwardian levels of inequality are almost fetishised.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From re- +‎ strain.

quote.citation: 1998, Elena Molokhovets, Classic Russian Cooking, page 360:
quote.text: Squeeze the juice from 3 oranges and let the juice stand. Then pour it off, strain, and mix with the syrup. Restrain the liquid and chill in a mold.
